statement: Find the first four terms in the expansion of $(1+x)^{1/2}$ in ascending powers of $x$, and hence estimate $\sqrt{1.02}$.
solution:
The binomial expansion gives
$$(1+x)^{1/2}=1+\tfrac12x+\frac{(\tfrac12)(-\tfrac12)}{2!}x^2+\frac{(\tfrac12)(-\tfrac12)(-\tfrac32)}{3!}x^3+\cdots=1+\tfrac12x-\tfrac18x^2+\tfrac1{16}x^3+\cdots.$$
Now $\sqrt{1.02}=(1.02)^{1/2}$ corresponds to $x=0.02$:
$$\sqrt{1.02}\approx 1+\tfrac12(0.02)-\tfrac18(0.02)^2+\tfrac1{16}(0.02)^3=1+0.01-0.00005+0.0000005\approx1.00995.$$
